summary: Historical ResolvedRegionRecipe v1 replay exact-shape validation can execute attacker-controlled formatting before rejection. ResolvedRegionRecipeV1Internal.assertExactRecordShape iterates arbitrary keys and interpolates tostring(key) in the assertion message; a plain outer record containing a table key with a __tostring metamethod therefore runs that callback. This is the same no-execute boundary class already hardened in MaterialDNA. Add a callback-zero adversarial replay regression and classify non-string keys with type(key) (while retaining literal names for unknown string keys) without changing any accepted historical v1 identity/fingerprint semantics.
evidence: src/shared/Reality/ResolvedRegionRecipeV1Internal.luau assertExactRecordShape checks the record metatable, then for each key formats `{path} contains unknown schema key {tostring(key)}` when the key is non-string or unknown.
A table used as a key may itself carry a __tostring metamethod even when the enclosing serialized record has no metatable, so rejection can invoke user-provided code.
PR #280 already expands adversarial v1 replay validation but currently covers unknown string fields and nested record metatables, not hostile non-string key formatting.
GitHub review 4903746640 records this source finding alongside approval of PR #280's existing test delta.
